office: Arkansas Secretary of State 2026 (State Senator, District 33)
executiveSummary: Primary opponent dossier: long-tenure senator with deep election-law authorship (2021 six-bill package, 2023/2025 clusters), integrity/#1 ranking campaign frame, and GOP base alignment. Strengths: experience narrative, election-law specialization, pastoral identity. Weaknesses for Kelly contrast: county implementation gaps, direct-democracy restriction pattern, narrow 2026 runoff, rhetoric controversies. Kelly wins on SOS-as-service, CVSGF ledger transparency, and clerk partnership — not motive attacks.

whatTheyClaim.claim: Arkansas elections are secure / nationally ranked #1 (Heritage-style rankings cited on campaign)
whatTheyClaim.kellyRebuttalFrame: Ranking is not a substitute for clerk training dollars — show county ledger.

whatTheyClaim.claim: I wrote the election integrity laws that secured Arkansas after 2020
whatTheyClaim.kellyRebuttalFrame: Security yes — six bills in one year shifted burden to counties without visible support package.

whatTheyClaim.sourceHint: Campaign trail; ACCA panel likely repeat

whatTheyClaim.claim: Poll watchers and transparency at the polls
whatTheyClaim.kellyRebuttalFrame: Observation with standards — clerks need SOS rulebooks and training, not precinct referee duty.

whatTheyClaim.claim: Stop fraud in petition drives / tighten signature rules
whatTheyClaim.kellyRebuttalFrame: Show fraud cases that justified each rule change; integrity + lawful participation together.
